login.title: Enter your PIN
login.lock_info: After 5 wrong tries, the dashboard locks for 15 minutes.
login.locked: Too many wrong tries. Try again at {time}.
setpin.title: Choose your own PIN
setpin.text: Replace the PIN you received with 4 digits only your household knows.
setpin.mismatch: The two PINs are not the same.
setpin.weak: This PIN is too easy to guess. Please choose another one.
setpin.same: Please choose a PIN different from the one you received.
recover.title: Forgot your PIN?
recover.text: Enter the recovery code you emailed to yourself, then choose a new PIN.
recover.wrong: This recovery code is not correct.
recover.lost: Lost the recovery code too? Take the SD card out of Bouncer and open it on a computer. Create a text file named bouncer-reset-pin.txt containing PIN=1234 (with your new PIN instead of 1234). Put the card back and plug Bouncer in again.
code.title: Save your recovery code
code.text: If you ever forget your PIN, this code lets you choose a new one. It is shown only once.
code.email_note: Opens your own email app. Nothing is sent by Bouncer.
code.done: I saved it, open the dashboard
code.mail_body:
My Bouncer recovery code is: {code}

If I forget my PIN, I open http://bouncer.local, tap "Forgot your PIN?" and enter this code.
theme.toggle: Switch between light and dark mode
status.on_text: Bouncer protects every device in your home that uses it.
status.paused_text: Nothing is blocked right now. Protection turns back on by itself.
pill.router_ok: Your router sends all devices through Bouncer
pill.address_mode: Bouncer hands out the network addresses
pill.router_forwards: Your router forwards all requests to Bouncer
pill.router_not_set: Your router does not use Bouncer yet
pill.router_secondary: Bouncer is only the second DNS server
notice.not_set_title: One step left: tell your router to use Bouncer
notice.not_set_text: Your devices still use your internet provider's DNS, so nothing is blocked yet.
notice.step2: Enter Bouncer's address as DNS server:
notice.step3: Turn Wi-Fi off and on on your devices (or wait a few hours). This page turns green.
notice.ipv6_text: Your router still tells devices to use itself over IPv6, so some requests skip Bouncer. In the router's IPv6 settings, enter Bouncer's IPv6 address as DNS server:
notice.forward_text: Blocking works, but Bouncer can't tell your devices apart. If your router allows it, set Bouncer as DNS server for the home network instead (see the router guide), or use address mode in Advanced settings.
notice.unprotected_text: Devices marked "Not protected" use their own DNS settings or haven't reconnected since the router change. Restart them or turn their Wi-Fi off and on.
notice.secondary_title: Make Bouncer the only DNS server
notice.secondary_text: Your router lists Bouncer only as a second DNS server, so many requests skip it. In the router, enter Bouncer as the first (or only) DNS server.
notice.waiting_text: Bouncer hasn't received requests from your devices yet. If you just changed the router setting, turn Wi-Fi off and on on a device.
num.blocked_hint: Requests to ad, tracking and scam servers that were stopped.
num.share_hint: Out of every 100 requests, {n} were stopped.
num.total_hint: A request is a device asking for a website or an app server.
num.saved_hint: Estimate. Fewer ads means less to download.
prot.title: What Bouncer blocks
prot.ads_text: Blocks ads and tracking on websites, apps and smart TVs.
prot.scam_text: Blocks known fake shops, phishing and dangerous websites.
prot.family_text: Safe search on Google, Bing and YouTube. Blocks adult websites.
chart.aria: Bar chart: {b} blocked and {a} allowed requests in this period.
speed.title: Speed check
speed.saved: About {mb} MB less data per page.
speed.running: Checking… this takes about a minute.
speed.never: Bouncer loads a few popular news websites with and without blocking and compares the time.
speed.last: Last check: {time}. Results vary by page and time of day.
dev.title: Devices
dev.hint: Names come from your router. Use Rename to change them.
dev.none: No devices yet. They appear as soon as they use Bouncer.
fix.title: A website doesn't work?
fix.text: Bouncer can unblock what it just blocked on one device, without showing any website names.
fix.step1: Open the broken website on that device.
fix.step2: Within 2 minutes, choose the device here and press Fix.
fix.done: Done: {n} blocked items were unblocked on this device. Reload the website.
fix.nothing: Nothing was blocked on this device in the last 2 minutes. Open the website again, then retry.
recent.title: Recent activity
recent.hint: What Bouncer blocked recently. Website names are hidden for privacy.
recent.scam: Blocked a scam or dangerous website
sys.software_hint: Updates install by themselves at night.
sys.update_failed: A new version failed its self-test and was not kept.
sys.lists_hint: Updated automatically every week. Last update: {when}.
sys.restore_failed: This file is not a Bouncer backup.
sys.faq: Why are YouTube ads not blocked?
adv.title: Advanced settings
adv.router_text: Enter these in your router as DNS server. The router guide explains where.
adv.am_text: Only for routers that can't change the DNS server (for example the Orange Livebox). First switch off the DHCP server in your router, then turn this on. Bouncer then hands out the network addresses itself.
adv.am_router_dhcp: Your router still hands out addresses. Switch off its DHCP server first, then try again.
adv.am_error: That didn't work. Please download diagnostics and send them to your Bouncer contact.
adv.am_confirm_text: Only continue if you have switched off the DHCP server in your router. Bouncer keeps its current address.
adv.am_disable_text: Switch the DHCP server in your router back on first, otherwise devices won't get an address.
adv.rules_text: Always allow or always block a website, including all its subdomains.
adv.clear_confirm: All statistics and the activity history will be deleted. Settings stay as they are.
adv.upstream_encrypted: Requests to the internet are encrypted (DNS over TLS via Quad9 and Cloudflare).
adv.upstream_plain: Encrypted DNS isn't reachable in this network. Requests are sent unencrypted for now; Bouncer retries regularly.
adv.upstream_none: No internet DNS server is reachable right now.
faq.title: What Bouncer can and can't block
faq.youtube: YouTube ads come from the same servers as the videos. Blocking them would also block the videos, so Bouncer can't remove them. On a computer, the free uBlock Origin extension for Firefox removes them; on other devices, only YouTube Premium does.
faq.apps: The same applies to ads inside Instagram, Facebook, TikTok and Spotify.
faq.guest: Devices on your router's guest Wi-Fi are usually not protected, because guest networks use the router's own DNS.
error: Something went wrong. Please try again.
offline: Bouncer can't be reached. Is it plugged in?
status.not_active_text: Bouncer is ready, but your router doesn't send your devices to it yet.
